title: Observed-execution verification: VERIFY v2 writer, retained outputs and a pre-merge CI run (GAP-0010 first slice)
created_from: GAP-0010 recommended first slice; step 2 of the five-step programme recorded in GAP-0005 (working order approved by the operator 2026-11-23, authorizing no step).
objective: Make it possible for a VERIFY record to state what a mechanism observed rather than what an executor reported: a writer that runs declared commands itself in a clean checkout of one exact commit, retains their output bytes under content addresses, records environment, verifier and input versions and the property each command is declared to establish, and a CI workflow that runs the same writer on the candidate merge commit of a pull request before merge. The plan produces evidence only; it authorizes and automates no decision.
proposed_change: Add VERIFY schema v2 beside v1 (v1 validator path, writer and 39 records unchanged) as a two-level contract: a writer receipt stored verbatim and a canonical VERIFY record derived from it; add scripts/verify_v2.py, a declared verification profile that audits before it rebuilds, a content-addressed store, an integrity checker and an importer that is the single path from receipt to record; add .github/workflows/verify-v2.yml running the writer on pull requests and on pushes to main with read-only permissions, no secrets and failure-path upload; add falsification and integration tests; document v2 in SELF_MODEL_SCHEMA.md.
scope: S1. Two-level record contract. (a) Receipt: the writer's raw output, a JSON document with no VERIFY id, stored verbatim in the content-addressed store and identified by the SHA-256 of its bytes. It carries: observation_basis 'observed_by_writer', meaning the producer's claim of observation and nothing more; subject (candidate_commit as full 40-hex, its git tree id, and for a pull request also head_sha, base_sha and the pull request number as reported by the runner); history (whether the checkout is shallow, and whether the index's stored repo_head is reachable from the subject commit); verifier (running_sha256, the SHA-256 of the writer bytes actually executing; subject_blob_sha, the git blob of scripts/verify_v2.py at the subject commit, or absent; verifier_matches_subject true, false or 'absent_at_subject'; interpreter path and version); inputs (git tree ids of the subject commit and of tests/, scripts/ and ai_lab/, and the profile path inside the subject tree with its content SHA-256); environment, labelled environment_capture 'partial' because it does not supply the full effective-input coverage of ABS-0004 Section 4.7 (python implementation and version, platform, SHA-256 of requirements.txt, SHA-256 of the sorted installed-distribution list with the list retained, the names and values of the allowlisted variables passed to commands, runner kind 'local' or 'github_actions' and, for the latter, run id, run attempt, workflow file SHA-256 and runner image, all as reported by the runner); started_at and finished_at for the run; commands, per S2; result and output_retention, per S2; verifier_lineage_status, always 'self_authored_unreviewed'. (b) Canonical VERIFY v2 record: a VERIFY-YYYYMMDD-NNNN file whose name matches its id, with the fields every VERIFY record shares: schema_version 'v2', verification_id, repo_commit, recorded_by naming the importing executor under the existing recorded_by rules, created_at as the import time; plus observed_at, receipt (store path and SHA-256), a summary block (result, output_retention, and per command the declared property, termination and exit code), origin (the runner the receipt claims, with origin_verification), and import (importer content SHA-256 and import time). (c) Invariants checked on every v2 record, never copied from the receipt: the receipt's result and output_retention are recomputed from its command entries by the S2 function and must equal the stored values; the record's summary must equal the summary recomputed from the receipt; repo_commit equals receipt.subject.candidate_commit; observed_at equals receipt.finished_at; origin_verification equals 'unverified'; verifier_lineage_status equals 'self_authored_unreviewed'; every store path equals the path derived from its digest and resolves inside the store root; the receipt bytes hash to the recorded SHA-256. Checks that need the store take the repository root as an explicit argument passed by the registry and audit paths; no check resolves a path from the process working directory. v1 records are unchanged and read as attributed_testimony; no v1 file is rewritten.

S2. Writer scripts/verify_v2.py, standard library only and importing nothing from ai_lab, so that the verifier's identity is one file. Arguments: --commit (full 40-hex only), --profile (a path relative to the subject tree), --store-root, --receipt-out and an explicit --foreign-verifier switch; no argument accepts an exit code, output, summary or result. It creates a detached git worktree of the commit in a temporary directory and reads the profile from that worktree, never from the invoking clone, refusing a profile path that is absolute, escapes the worktree or is absent at the subject, and refusing an empty profile. By default it refuses to run when its own bytes differ from scripts/verify_v2.py at the subject commit; with --foreign-verifier it runs and records verifier_matches_subject false or 'absent_at_subject'. Each profile command runs in the worktree root without a shell, with the interpreter token resolved to the writer's own interpreter and a {scratch} token resolved to a per-run directory outside the worktree, and with a positive, finite timeout declared per command in the profile and recorded. Commands receive only an allowlisted environment: PATH, a fresh empty HOME, LANG, TZ and the variables the profile declares; nothing else from the writer's environment, including provider API keys, tokens and proxy settings, reaches a command or the receipt. The receipt records the template argv, the resolved argv, the working directory and the timeout. Per command it records termination ('exited', 'timeout', 'signal' or 'failed_to_start'), exit_code (an integer only when termination is 'exited', otherwise null), start and finish times, and for stdout and stderr the observed byte count, the retained bytes' SHA-256 and store path, and capture_complete. Each stream is retained up to 8 MiB; beyond that the first 8 MiB are kept, capture_complete is false and the observed total is recorded, so a truncated stream is never presented as full; output_retention is 'complete' when every stream is complete and 'partial' otherwise. Tree observation: before the first command and after every command the writer snapshots git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all --ignored in the worktree, so tracked, untracked and ignored paths are all observed, and records per command whether the snapshot changed and which paths changed; VPROF-0001 permits no change. The observation is made at command boundaries only: a path changed and restored within one command is not detected, and the receipt says so. Result, a deterministic function with this precedence: 'incomplete' when C fails or D holds, where C is that the profile is non-empty, every command terminated by exiting and every required field of the receipt was recorded, and D is that any snapshot after any command, first, intermediate or last, differs from the snapshot before the first command outside the paths the profile permits; otherwise 'one_or_more_commands_failed' when some exit code is non-zero; otherwise 'all_commands_exit_zero'. 'incomplete' is never a success. The writer removes the worktree on every path and exits non-zero unless the result is 'all_commands_exit_zero'. It installs nothing.

S3. Profile docs/self_model/verification_profiles/VPROF-0001.json, the standard triple, in this order, each with a declared timeout, with the profile-declared environment variable PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 and no permitted tree changes: (1) audit_self_model_index.py on the unmodified worktree: 'the self-model index committed at the subject commit audits ok and verified_current against the records and git history available at the subject commit'; (2) build_self_model.py with --output {scratch}/SELF_MODEL.rebuilt.json: 'an index can be rebuilt from the subject commit's records without error'; the tracked index is not overwritten and the rebuilt file is not compared by this command; (3) pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider: 'the test suite at the subject commit passes in the recorded environment'. Running the audit first and redirecting the build keeps every command's property about the committed tree (reviewing-executor counterexample: a stale committed index passes after an in-place rebuild). Suppressing bytecode and the pytest cache is what makes 'no permitted change' satisfiable: measured by the packaging executor at 88c9d45, the unsuppressed triple wrote __pycache__ during the audit alone and several hundred cache and bytecode paths during pytest, while the suppressed triple under the S2 allowlisted environment left zero changed paths (tracked, untracked or ignored) with 925 passed; this is testimony until the first receipt observes it. Declared properties are P2-scoped declarations of what each command is relied on to establish; the writer does not check that a command tests its declared property. Tests that exercise the writer use small fixture repositories and fixture profiles, never the standard triple, so the suite does not invoke itself recursively.

S4. Content-addressed store docs/self_model/verification_outputs/sha256/<first two hex>/<digest> holding retained output bytes and receipts, and scripts/check_verification_outputs.py, which recomputes the SHA-256 of every blob a v2 record or receipt references and reports missing blobs and mismatches. Integrity means stored bytes equal the recorded digest; it does not establish where or whether a run took place. Deduplication does not bound growth for variable output; the per-stream limit of S2 does, and growth is measured. A re-run is a separate receipt; two runs are compared only on declared properties, and byte equality is expected only where an output contract requires it.

S5. CI workflow .github/workflows/verify-v2.yml. Triggers: pull_request and push to main. Checks out the event commit with fetch-depth 0, because the audit needs the stored repo_head and the history since it, and with persist-credentials false, so that no token remains in the checkout; sets up Python 3.12, installs requirements.txt, runs the writer against that commit, uploads the receipt and its stored outputs as a workflow artifact in a step conditioned on always() so that a failed or incomplete run still uploads what exists, and leaves the job failed whenever the writer exits non-zero. Permissions: contents read; no secrets; third-party actions pinned to full commit SHAs resolved at implementation time; the workflow file's SHA-256 enters the receipt (Section 4.7 tool-configuration disclosure). The artifact is transport, not retention: GitHub deletes artifacts after the repository's retention period, 90 days by default, or with their run; only import makes a receipt durable. Coverage contract, with M_PR the synthetic merge commit a pull_request run tests, M_main the commit that actually enters main and I the commit that imports a receipt: a receipt covers only its subject; M_PR = M_main is not assumed; M_PR need not be an ancestor of I and is not retained by the repository, which is why the receipt records its tree id with head_sha and base_sha; a push-to-main run produces separate evidence for M_main and is never counted retroactively as pre-merge evidence; the presence of a receipt in I says nothing about I. content_equivalence: tree(A) = tree(B) establishes equality of git-tracked content only. It is not equality of verification scope, because the standard profile's audit also depends on git history (the HEAD, the reachability of the stored repo_head and the paths changed since it), so the same tree with a different history can audit differently. The tree comparison is recorded under that name and is not to be used by any later acceptance mechanism as sufficient coverage of M_main by a receipt for M_PR.

S6. Importer scripts/import_verification_v2.py, the single path by which any receipt, local or CI, becomes a canonical VERIFY v2 record. It accepts a producer's receipt and says so: it validates the receipt schema, re-checks every blob digest, stores the receipt verbatim, derives the summary from the receipt, assigns the next free VERIFY id for the import date, and writes the canonical record with origin_verification 'unverified'. It does not establish that the claimed run took place: a self-consistent receipt with a fabricated run id and matching digests passes its checks, and the record represents that. It refuses to import a receipt whose SHA-256 is already referenced by an existing VERIFY record, never overwrites an existing file, and keeps the receipt's observation time and producer distinct from the import time and importing executor.

S7. Falsification tests under tests/ (zero-API, run in the standard suite, using fixture repositories and fixture profiles): F1 no writer argument accepts an exit code, output, summary or result; F2 a failing command yields termination 'exited', its exit code, result 'one_or_more_commands_failed' and a non-zero writer exit; F3 an abbreviated, unresolvable or mismatching commit is refused, and uncommitted changes in the invoking clone do not reach the worktree; F4 altering a stored blob or a recorded digest is detected by the checker; F5 a profile is read from the subject tree, so editing it in the invoking clone changes nothing, and an absolute, escaping, absent or empty profile is refused; F6 the worktree is removed after success, failure and incomplete runs; F7 every v1 record still validates, and a v2 record lacking any required block is refused; F8 the writer never emits a verifier_lineage_status stronger than 'self_authored_unreviewed'; F9 the importer refuses a receipt whose blob digests do not match, a receipt already imported, and an id that would overwrite a file; F10 a stale committed index makes a triple-shaped fixture profile fail even though its build command succeeds; F11 a writer whose bytes differ from the subject's refuses by default, and with --foreign-verifier records verifier_matches_subject false; F12 a timed-out, signalled or unstartable command yields result 'incomplete' with a null exit code and never a success; F13 a stream over the retention limit yields capture_complete false, the observed total and output_retention 'partial'; F14 a change by the first, an intermediate and the last command, each of a tracked, an untracked and an ignored path, yields result 'incomplete' even when every exit code is zero; F15 a static check of the workflow file finds the upload step conditioned on always(), no continue-on-error on the writer step, contents read permission, fetch-depth 0 and persist-credentials false; F16 (integration) a temporary repository holding the 39 v1 records, one local v2 record and one CI-shaped v2 record passes registry loading, index build and audit together, invoked from the repository root and from an unrelated working directory; F17 each S1(c) invariant is violated in turn, including a receipt carrying exit code 1 with result 'all_commands_exit_zero', and each violation is refused even when the record's summary matches the receipt; F18 a variable outside the allowlist, such as a fake provider API key set in the writer's environment, neither reaches a command nor appears in the receipt.

S8. SELF_MODEL_SCHEMA.md VERIFY section: receipt and canonical record, the v1 and v2 difference stated as testimony versus a producer's claim of observation, the store, the importer and what it does not establish, and the coverage contract of S5. VERIFICATION_OUTCOMES.md unchanged.

S9. First live use, imported in the completion changeset with lineage as written: one local receipt for the implementation commit; one CI receipt for the implementation pull request's merge commit; and one deliberately failing CI run on a throwaway branch whose commit breaks one test, observed to upload its receipt and leave the job failed, and imported with result 'one_or_more_commands_failed' as live falsification of the failure path.
non_goals: No automated acceptance, merge, warrant, plan admission or status transition, and no decision of any kind taken on the strength of a v2 record.

No branch protection, ruleset, required status check or CODEOWNERS change: those are extra-systemic arrangements of the operator. Completing this plan does not close GAP-0010's required-check dimension, which stays open.

No attestation of CI origin, no IndependenceAssessment, no review artifact that could raise verifier_lineage_status, and no claim that the writer is independent of the code it verifies: the packaging executor authors both.
No C7 implementer and verifier pair; that is GAP-0005's first slice, to be carried on v2 records in a later plan.

No capability last_verified change pointing at a v2 record in this plan; a capability citing a CI receipt whose subject is a synthetic merge commit would meet the audit's commit-existence check, which a later plan must address.
No rewriting, re-labelling or deletion of v1 records or of scripts/write_verification_record.py, and no upgrade of any v1 record to observed status.
No change to tool or cross-kind executor equivalence (step 3) and no change to ABS-0004.
No dependency change to requirements.txt; the socksio case is handled by recording the environment, not by adding a dependency.
constraints: Implementation is authorized only within scope S1 to S9 as admitted by a future admission warrant; any expansion requires a separate proposed and admitted plan.
The v1 validator path accepts every existing v1 record without change; the suite proves it (F7).

The writer's execution interface accepts no result supplied by a caller; every result in a receipt is produced by the run it describes. The importer accepts a producer's receipt, checks schema and byte integrity, and records that the receipt's origin is unverified.
verifier_lineage_status is written as 'self_authored_unreviewed' and nothing in this plan can raise it.
The workflow runs with contents read permission, no secrets and no write-back to the repository; receipts become records only through the importer.
Standard staging order holds: records, then build_self_model.py, then the suite; the pre-commit hook stays installed in the packaging executor's clone.

Raw outputs imported into this public repository become public; the S2 environment allowlist keeps secrets out of commands and receipts, and the importer refuses a receipt whose recorded environment contains a variable outside the allowlist.
success_criteria: S7 tests F1 to F18 pass, and each falsification test was observed to fail against a deliberately broken variant before reliance.
The full suite passes with all 39 v1 records validating unchanged; the index audit reports ok and verified_current.

The first local receipt under VPROF-0001 observes zero changed paths and result 'all_commands_exit_zero', or the plan reports otherwise and does not proceed to S9's CI runs until the difference is understood.
The three S9 receipts are imported; their stored blobs pass the checker; the failing CI run is observed to have uploaded its receipt with the job failed.

For the implementation pull request, the completion summary states the content_equivalence of M_main with the imported CI receipt's M_PR, labelled as tracked-content equality and not as verification-scope equality.
Stored bytes per standard-triple receipt are measured and reported in the completion summary, so repository growth is a recorded quantity.
expected_outputs: ai_lab/documentation/self_model.py (v2 validation path, summary recomputation) and tests.
docs/self_model/verification_outputs/ (content-addressed store of outputs and receipts).
Three v2 VERIFY records (local, CI pass, CI deliberate failure) in the completion changeset.
rationale: Every later step of the GAP-0005 programme needs evidence that a check ran on the exact candidate; without it, any delegated acceptance would rest on reported success.

The writer and the workflow are deliberately evidence-only: separating evidence production from any decision keeps this plan's consequence bounded to repository mutation and lets the decision machinery be reviewed separately in step 4.
Retaining output bytes under content addresses makes integrity checkable without re-running commands whose output is not byte-stable.
Recording the environment turns cases like the reviewer's socksio dependency into a visible difference between runs rather than an unexplained discrepancy.
Keeping v1 untouched preserves the historical record's standing as testimony; observation starts with the first v2 record and is not projected backwards.
risk: The writer could be mistaken for an independent verifier when the same executor authors it and much of the code it checks; a passing CI run could be read as acceptance; an imported CI receipt could be read as attested origin; a declared property could be read as established when only an exit code is observed; a command could alter the tree under later commands; a truncated or incomplete run could be read as complete; the store grows with every receipt; a receipt for a synthetic merge commit could be cited for a different merged commit; the workflow could be weakened by a later change to its own file.
mitigation: Lineage is written as self_authored_unreviewed and cannot be raised; origin_verification is written as unverified; the non-goals exclude every decision; declared properties are labelled as declarations; the audit runs first and the build is redirected; any tracked, untracked or ignored change at any command boundary makes the result incomplete, and the boundary-only limit of that observation is stated; termination, timeouts, capture completeness and an 'incomplete' result are explicit and every derived field is recomputed by the validator; an environment allowlist keeps credentials out of commands and receipts; a per-stream limit bounds growth and growth is measured; content_equivalence is named as tracked-content equality and excluded as sufficient coverage; the workflow fetches full history without persisting credentials and its file digest is recorded in every CI receipt. Protecting .github/ is an operator arrangement recorded in GAP-0005 and outside this plan.
next_action: S1-S9 are complete under WARR-20261125-0001, recording the PI's acceptance of package 86f08b3f9f3192bfe576d5be207752e446af5941. Proceed only to preparation of programme step 3: separate the tool/human equivalence tests, governed cross-kind semantics, the open ExecutorIdentity-superclass decision, and executable C3/C10 evidence conditions into reviewable scope. This completion does not admit that implementation; any implementation or ontology change requires its own review and admission. GAP-0010, GAP-0005 and GAP-0008 remain open, writer-PI identity separation remains unresolved, and no autonomy is activated.
notes: Drafted outside the tracked tree against HEAD 88c9d45 (clean) by the packaging executor (claude-opus-5-5, declared) and validated with validate_plan_record before submission for review.
Consequence class: plan admission is high under ABS-0004 Section 8; the implementation is a repository mutation adding a workflow, three scripts, a profile, a store and a validator path.

Under C10 every v2 record this plan produces has a verifier authored by the packaging executor; where the subject commit also contains packaging-executor code, the lineage is self-authored in the C10 sense for that run, and the record says so.

Under C7 the packaging executor will implement this plan; it is not to be the sole verifier of its own changes: the reviewing executor's verification and the operator's admission remain required, as for every plan before delegation exists.

Revision r2 (2026-11-24) after reviewing-executor round 1 (CHANGES_REQUESTED). R1: the reviewing executor ran a counterexample at 88c9d45 in which a committed index with open gaps set to 999 audited stale, then passed build, the suite and the audit after the in-place rebuild; S3 now audits first and redirects the build. R2: the running writer is bound to the subject's writer by default and the profile is read from the subject tree. R3: the importer is stated as accepting a producer's receipt with unverified origin. R4: receipt and canonical record are separated, with common fields, id assignment, re-import refusal and an integration test. R5: termination, capture completeness, an incomplete result and failure-path artifact upload are defined. The reviewing executor's answers on the two design questions are adopted: content-addressed storage in git for this slice with a per-stream limit, CI artifacts as transport only, and the M_PR, M_main, I distinction.

Added by the packaging executor in r2, beyond the review: the audit checks commit existence only for capability evidence commits and capability last_verified.repo_commit, so a CI v2 record whose subject is a synthetic merge commit passes today's audit but could not be cited as a capability's last verification without SELF_MODEL_VERIFICATION_COMMIT_MISSING; this plan therefore records subject tree ids and makes no last_verified change.

Revision r3 (2026-11-24) after reviewing-executor round 2 (CHANGES_REQUESTED; R1 to R3 closed, R4 and R5 to be completed). R6: the result is a total function with the precedence incomplete, then failed, then success; per-command timeouts are restored; tree observation covers tracked, untracked and ignored paths at every command boundary, including after the last command, with the boundary-only limit stated. R7: every derived field is recomputed rather than copied, the listed invariants are checked, and store checks take an explicit repository root. R8: tree equality is named content_equivalence and excluded as verification-scope equality; the workflow checks out with fetch-depth 0 and persist-credentials false. The reviewer's implementation notes are adopted: a pull request for the failing throwaway branch, fixture repositories with no recursive suite invocation, no credentials passed to commands, care for raw outputs in a public repository, and partial environment capture.

Measured by the packaging executor in r3, beyond the review: applying R6's rule to the untracked and ignored paths as well would have made the unsuppressed standard triple always incomplete, because the audit alone writes __pycache__ and pytest writes several hundred cache and bytecode paths. With PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 and pytest -p no:cacheprovider under an allowlisted environment (PATH, a fresh HOME, LANG, TZ) the triple left zero changed paths with 925 passed at 88c9d45, so VPROF-0001 can permit no change at all rather than carry an allowlist of paths. The same minimal environment contains no proxy variables, which bears on the reviewer's socksio case.
